# Surrogate vs Natural Keys

A **natural key** is the identifier the source system already uses — a product id, a customer id, an
order-line id. A **surrogate key** is a meaningless integer the warehouse mints itself, usually with
`IDENTITY` or a sequence. Standard Kimball practice prefers surrogates in dimensions, because they
insulate the warehouse from source-system renumbering and because Type-2 history needs one row per
version of an entity and a natural key cannot be unique across versions.

## The contrast inside one repository

[[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] does it both ways, in two marts built by the same
author, which is what makes the trade-off legible rather than theoretical.

| | Retail mart | Price mart |
|---|---|---|
| `DIM_PRODUCT` / `DIM_CUSTOMER` / `DIM_SALESPERSON` | **natural** — the source ids are the PKs | — |
| `DIM_TIME` / `DIM_DATE` | **smart natural** — `yyyymmdd` as an `INT` | same convention |
| `DIM_TICKER` | — | **surrogate** — `TickerKey INT IDENTITY(1,1)`, with `Symbol` kept `UNIQUE` |
| Fact PK | the source order-line id, a **degenerate** key | composite of the two dimension keys |

`DIM_TICKER` is the only true surrogate in the repository. It also carries `ListedOn` / `DelistedOn`
— a hand-rolled validity window that is the closest thing to slowly-changing-dimension handling
anywhere in the repo, and it is populated by a single hard-coded row.

## The date key is the interesting middle case

`CONVERT(INT, CONVERT(CHAR(8), d.[Date], 112))` produces `20240115`. It is natural (derivable from
the date), surrogate-shaped (a compact integer that joins fast), and human-readable in a query plan
— which is why the `yyyymmdd` integer is near-universal for calendar dimensions and is used in both
marts here.

## What the absence of surrogates costs here

Because every load is truncate-and-rebuild, the usual argument for surrogates — supporting Type-2
history — never has to be made. **There is no SCD handling in this repository at all**: no
`EffectiveFrom`/`EffectiveTo`, no `IsCurrent`, no version rows. Natural keys are adequate precisely
because history is not kept. That is a coupling worth naming: the key choice and the load strategy in
[[etl-load-order]] are the same decision seen from two sides. See also [[fact-grain]].
